oh_source.digest_note: canonical digest computed on a native LF checkout; a Windows autocrlf checkout yields CRLF variant 0327ce5c... — content conclusions unaffected
oh_source.gap_evidence: upstream fix 2026-08-28 postdates the 20260819 snapshot; no backport commit found (grep CVE id + recent log); OH's lib/cookie.c retains the pre-refactor PSL structure without the tailmatch-clearing logic at the psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable call site (line ~1049)

vulnerability.summary: With libpsl enabled, libcurl accepts a cookie whose Domain equals the request host when that host is itself a public suffix, keeping tailmatch=TRUE — a supercookie matching all subdomains of the suffix.
vulnerability.trigger: HTTP response to a request for a PSL-listed host (e.g. localhost) carrying Set-Cookie with Domain equal to that host.
vulnerability.machine_signal: CURLINFO_COOKIELIST entry for the PSL host: domain field with leading dot (tailmatch TRUE) = vulnerable; without dot = fixed. Equivalently in a Netscape-format jar, the leading-dot convention marks tailmatching.
vulnerability.fix_core: After psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable() accepts, clear co->tailmatch when the cookie domain is itself a public suffix (upstream 95c1e891, adapted to OH's pre-refactor structure).

controls.name: non-psl-domain
controls.desc: Set-Cookie Domain=sub.localhost (not a suffix): accepted with tailmatch on BOTH original and patched — must not regress

controls.name: psl-reject
controls.desc: Set-Cookie Domain=com for host x.example.com: rejected on BOTH (existing psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable behavior unchanged)

build_requirements: libcurl sources (OH tree) built with USE_LIBPSL; libpsl dev package; POSIX sockets (loopback only)
notes: patch.diff is ADAPTED to OH's pre-refactor structure (upstream's is_public_suffix wrapper does not exist there); the second upstream hunk (check reordering) is defense-in-depth and intentionally omitted from the narrow patch.
